gitobj.description: one Git object; its entity id is its SHA-1 object id, so writing the same object twice writes one row

type.description: the object type, as written in the object's own header

size.description: the body's length in bytes, as written in that same header

blob.description: where an object's bytes are: their address in the @yaks/blob store

sha.description: the SHA-256 of the bytes; for a Git blob this is the file's own address in the store, not a re-encoded copy. Indexed: a release names each new file's object by it

tree_entry.description: a retained tree-to-child link; traversal reads children from the immutable tree body

name.description: the child's name in this tree; one object can be a child of several trees under different names, so the name belongs to the link

mode.description: the mode as the tree body writes it: 100644 for a file, 40000 for a directory

parent.description: this commit's parent; the edge's `ord` property keeps the parent order

compat.description: Git's compat object id: the same object's SHA-256 id, keyed by its SHA-1 id, so a client may ask for either (Git's hash-function transition, stored as key rows)

ref.description: where one branch of one repository points; one row per repository and branch name, so moving a branch updates the row that is already there

app.description: the entity the repository belongs to; deleting it deletes its branches

name.description: the branch's full name: refs/heads/main, not main

commit.description: the commit object the branch points at

target.description: for a symbolic ref, the full name it points at; absent for a direct ref

oid.description: the raw Git object id the ref names; an annotated tag need not point directly at a commit

present.description: false once a ref that was observed on this machine has been deleted

repository.description: A Git object database identified by its stable filesystem workspace and canonical common directory.

common.description: canonical absolute common Git directory in the repository filesystem

origin.description: where it is published: the remote it was cloned from or pushes to

workspace.description: the stable filesystem context: its sandbox or the canonical root workspace of its computer, not a convenience directory

worktree.description: A local checkout. Its identity is the repository plus the canonical checkout root, not the branch or HEAD.

gitdir.description: this worktree's own Git administrative directory

head.description: the object id HEAD resolves to; absent when the branch has no commits yet

branch.description: the shared ref entity HEAD is attached to; absent for a detached HEAD

managed.description: created by this package; it never implies automatic cleanup

checkout.description: A stored request to create a checkout on this machine; ready only once Git has succeeded. A failed request keeps its error so it can be retried.

requested.description: the base as the caller wrote it, while base holds the commit id it resolved to

target.description: the work this commit is about

message.description: the whole commit message, not just its first line

commit.description: a commit that landed, attached to the work it is about; the commit sha is the entity id, so recording the same commit twice gives one entity
the commit entity, whose id is the commit sha

revision.description: the commit a citation was last checked against; the verify step moves it to the commit checked out then

cites_check.title: Check citations
cites_check.description: Report citations that moved or were never checked. A `cites` edge points to a `file`, to some lines of one (an entity wearing `lines{file, start, end}`), to a symbol, or to any other graph entity. For a file of a repository, its lines or a symbol in it, Git answers in this checkout, which must be of that repository, which commits after `revision.commit` touched the cited place. For anything else, its current content hash is compared with `cites.hash`, recorded when verified; this needs no journal or checkout. A citation nobody checked is unverified, and one without enough evidence is unknown. Scope with `of` (only citations one entity makes) or `path` (only citations of one file of this checkout's repository: the file, lines of it, or a symbol in it). Returns a report in content.body with warning or failure findings. It writes nothing and enforces nothing.

of.description: only the citations this record makes; pass its id or registered name

path.description: only citations of this file of this checkout's repository, lines of it or a symbol in it; the path as Git spells it

cites_verify.title: Verify a citation
cites_verify.description: Record that a citation was checked and holds. For a file of a repository, lines of one or a symbol, write the `verified` mark and move its `revision` to this checkout's commit; the checkout must be of that repository. For another entity, write the mark and its current content hash in `cites.hash`, without needing a checkout. Takes the citation edge itself, or an entity, meaning every citation it makes. Returns the citations as written.

cite.description: the citation to mark; pass its id

of.description: a record, meaning every citation it makes

land.title: Land the current branch
land.description: Land the branch the current checkout is on. Fast-forwards it into the base branch (the one the shared checkout has checked out) and pushes if the base has an upstream. If the base has moved, rebases the branch onto it and returns without merging, printing what the rebase pulled in so the caller can re-run its tests and land again; that counts as a failure, because nothing landed. Refuses to land when a file would end up with content no commit on the branch wrote, unless allow-revert names that file. Runs no tests: everything comes from Git, in the checkout explicitly named by cwd. Records each commit it lands as `commit{target, message}`, its id the sha, created through the caller's session, its target the task its first line names (T-12). The CLI supplies its current directory; MCP callers must name their own checkout, including sub-agents sharing a connection. Returns Git’s output and the landed commit SHA in content.body.

cwd.description: absolute working directory of the checkout to land; supply your own checkout even on a shared MCP connection

allow-revert.description: comma-separated paths whose reverted content is intended; they land with a warning

commit.description: a commit that landed, attached to the work it is about; the commit sha is the entity id, so recording the same commit twice gives one entity
